title: Why the band changed: bebop and the closing ballrooms
summary: They conclude it was a transition, with bebop, better-paid sidemen, and ballrooms closing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: See, Stanley, what I would like to ask Freddie, and I don't know if Freddie can answer it, but what I'm really getting at -- and we know that through the war years --
Mm hmm.
-- there had to be alot of changes.
Oh, yeah.

And, then did it just take change that way -- guys changed? Or, I know Duke also had some troubles. I guess alot of people had troubles after that. I mean, here's a band that's stuck together, you know, for years --
Mm hmm.
-- and now it's just a succession of changes. Is it the times or is it -- it's just altered. It isn't a family anymore.
It might have been the times. I really don't know. I can't put my hand on it, because I don't remember.
People were restless, or --. No. No. But, I mean, that's a tremendous lot of changes. One year after another it's nothing but
changes, isn't it?
Well, I think the band was going through a transition, then, you know.
Yeah. Yeah. People were going through a transition then.
Right. And, it was happening over here, you know.
Yeah.
And, the ones that left -- I can't put my hand on the reason they left.
Yeah.
Because I've never -- as I say I've never put myself in that position to --
Even being there as long as I have.
Yeah.
But, I think too, you know, because of the war -- you know -- some of these side men were in demand --
Mm hmm.
-- and they were probably going for better money.
That could be. That could be it.
But, you see Paul Gershalves had been in the Army.
Mm hmm.
He came out.
Yeah. Well, I mean -- so -- in any case, I mean, Dizzy and Charlie Parker had got their thing going -- things were altering.
That was another change.
You know -- times were changing --
Times were changing.
-- and people were going around saying -- "Well, what once was was what once was and now what are they coming up with?" and so on.
Mm hmm. Something new.
Yeah. Something new. And, people were saying "Well, is it good enough to keep doing what you're doing?". Do you remember? I mean people were [~~]
Mm hmm.
You know, plenty of people were saying "what Basie does is what Basie does, which is wonderful, and that's how things should be". But, I guess there was alot of conflict like that.
Well, the other thing is that the ball rooms.
That's right.
They'd closed down.
That's right.
The dance thing. That's right.
That's right.
Yeah -- dancing was out.
And there were more concerts and there wasn't the same thing for dancing.
Right.
Yeah. I guess that whole--
These are things in which the whole format -- was a transition, more or less.
That's right. That's right. That does alot to
explain it.
I mean, when somebody cuts it down to a small group -- I mean, it's really a matter -- it must have been a matter of economics.

Yeah. Evidently it was -- it wound up that way -- with all the changes happening, and then all of a sudden they said 'let's chop it off'. Evidently, because in the '50's it was like, you know, a small group. They cut it down to a small group.
